Order No.03 Dated- 13.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1158 of 2023, instituted under Sections 323, 341, 379, 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

As per the F.I.R, it is alleged that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the present petitioner on 15.05.2019 with Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the parents of the complainant gifted cash of Rs.4,51,000/- and other household article worth Rs.3,00,000/-.

The Complainant lived peacefully for one year and she gave birth to a female child and in regard to the birth of female child she was being tortured and assaulted by her husband, mother-in-law and other co-accused persons for demand of additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/- and ousted from the house.
Several times oral Panchayati were convened but in vain.
To settle the matter, parents of the complainant arranged Rs.50,000/- and was given to the accused persons.
But, again on 05.03.2023 she was tortured and mother-in-law of the complainant snatched the mangal sutra from her neck and ousted from the house.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the entire allegations are false and concocted story.
Petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
